cleanup.evidence: Scope was established before the run rather than argued after it. The CTP shell helpers run `cubrid service stop` and an unscoped `pkill cub` in init and finish, and sweep every System V segment this UNIX user owns in release_broker_sharedmemory; the whole invocation therefore ran inside `unshare --user --map-current-user --pid --fork --mount-proc --ipc`, which makes processes and IPC segments outside the invocation unaddressable rather than merely protected. isolation_check.sh demonstrates this with two matched pairs -- a cub-named process and a System V segment created outside survive the same sweep that kills and destroys their counterparts created inside -- so the containment check is shown to discriminate; it passed with failures=0 on this host before the run (isolation/isolation.txt). The case's own crash step is additionally scoped: it snapshots the cub_master pids that already exist before it starts anything and kills only masters absent from that snapshot, so it is safe even outside the namespace. This run's operations.journal records pre_existing_masters=[], which is the containment working: an unrelated cub_master and cub_server serving demodb (another session's, same UNIX user) ran on this host throughout and were invisible, untouched and still running afterwards (isolation/live-containment.txt). EVIDENCE BEFORE CLEANUP: the first failed assertion captures processes, journals, server status and the CUBRID logs, and cleanup copies the recovered database and the server logs aside before deleting them. That is not decorative -- this case sets SKIP_CHECK_RECOVERY_ERROR=TRUE on its post-crash `cubrid server start` and `checkdb`, which switches off CTP's own installation-snapshot channel, so without it a failed value assertion would leave nothing but a result line. Every copy step is checked and a failed copy is reported as a further NOK, so a lost image cannot be silent. The negative control att-T14-0025 exercises the path: it journalled preservation|ok and preserved a 259 MiB database image plus an 88 KiB first-failure snapshot. Two further scope items, both verified by hashing before and after: CTP rewrites $CUBRID/conf from ~/.CUBRID_SHELL_FM and writes its ports into cubrid.conf, cubrid_broker.conf and cubrid_ha.conf, so HOME was redirected to a campaign-owned directory seeded from the pinned install and the install's conf and databases were restored verbatim afterwards (install_conf_drift_lines=0, install_databases_drift_lines=0); and the user's own ~/.CUBRID_SHELL_FM was neither read nor written (user_shell_fm_drift_lines=0). The case deletes its own database and leaves the testcase worktree with zero untracked files.

notes: The debug configuration of the same tracer bullet, run so that the capability-gated assertion the release run has to skip actually executes: all 17 assertions ran and passed, and the skip journal is empty. Two observations. (1) The debug oos.log already carried oos_delete lines from vacuum before the case's standalone evidence step, so on this build vacuum reclaimed the two dead chains within a few seconds of the restart; an earlier format probe on the same build saw nothing within three seconds. That is exactly why assertion 17 is written as an increase over the count taken immediately before the standalone update rather than as 'oos.log is non-empty': a durability case must not depend on vacuum timing. It is also a small piece of evidence for the reclaim tickets that the forward-walk runs promptly here. (2) SHOW HEAP OOS reported Oos_num_recs 5 after recovery, the top of this case's asserted 3..5 range: three live chunks plus the superseded chain of id=1 and the chain of the deleted id=4, neither reclaimed at the moment of the observation. Oos_recs_sumlen was 24444 after the insert, matching the pinned-layout derivation exactly (4044+16, 16292+32, 4044+16); it is recorded and never asserted, because the accepted 24-byte chunk header of CBRD-26950 would give 24476 and that divergence is the OOS-REP-05 Capability gap. REVISION 3, after both axes of the two-axis review. The Standards axis produced five fixes (generator moved into cases/ as a non-discovered helper, SKIP_CHECK_RECOVERY_ERROR on the post-crash start and checkdb, the skip line taking its own assertion number, a guard that never deletes a caller-supplied evidence directory, and oos_field taking a single row). The Spec axis produced four more, all fixed here: (i) THE ORACLE'S PROVENANCE CLAIM WAS WITHDRAWN -- probes/probe_format.sh had already run the case's own fixture, sizes, update, crash and restart before expected-oracle.md was written, so the oracle's independence rests on its derivation and not on the ordering, and the corrected text and probes/README.txt now say so; (ii) failure evidence is preserved before cleanup, as described in the cleanup field; (iii) the case's internal deadlines were lowered to 30 s and 60 s so that a run reaching both still finishes inside the declared 120 s per-case cap, which the previous 180 s restart deadline contradicted; (iv) the case now states a campaign outcome of its own, so a build without SHOW HEAP OOS records SKIP instead of a pass with no activation evidence. The Spec axis also confirmed independently that the derived sizes, the digests, the chunk counts, the non-discovery argument and the 'proven' evidence status all hold. Revisions 1 and 2 (att-T14-0001 to att-T14-0012-bucket) are retained as history and cited by no manifest. The declared deadline of 120 seconds is the campaign's fast-tier per-case cap. The case's own waits are 30 seconds for the killed processes to disappear and 60 seconds for the restart to answer a query, chosen so that a run which reaches both still finishes inside that cap; measured, they were under a second and about three seconds. REVISION 4: the failure-preservation copy is now checked step by step instead of discarding its errors, and a failed copy is reported as a further NOK. That was the Spec reviewer's one residual point after it verified revision 3, and it matters because with SKIP_CHECK_RECOVERY_ERROR=TRUE suppressing CTP's snapshot channel this copy is the only image a failing run leaves behind, so losing it silently is exactly the outcome this campaign exists to prevent. att-T14-0025 exercised the path and journalled preservation|ok. REVISION 5: the SHOW HEAP OOS output classifier now has three outcomes instead of two. The Standards reviewer's confirmation pass found that a catch-all made any non-syntax failure -- a disconnect, an authorization error, a renamed column, a class-name mismatch -- indistinguishable from 'this build lacks the statement', so a real failure would have been recorded as a capability gap and, because a SKIP line carries no NOK, the case would have passed with no activation evidence: the inverse of what this case is for. Only a syntax error now skips; anything else fails. Writing the controlled failure example for the new classifier then caught a second defect in the fix before it shipped -- matching the bare class name also matches `ERROR: Unknown class "dba.oos_dur01".`, so an error was read as an answer and fields were extracted from the error text. The shipped selector requires the quoted class name and the full column count, and feeds both the classification and the extraction so they cannot disagree. Seven cases in tools/checker_validation_classifier.sh, failures=0. REVISION 6: the activation channel's column positions are read from the output's own header instead of being hardcoded. The Standards confirmation pass established that NF >= 14 proves a row is wide enough but not that field 11 is still Oos_num_recs -- the order lives one line away in the engine's show_meta.c, and a reordering would have been read silently as has_oos=577 and chunks=16344, surfacing as a failure only because the two expected ranges happen to be narrow. A column the case needs that the header does not have is now a failure, not a capability gap. Writing the twelfth shape for the classifier's controlled failure example caught a shell-quoting error in that same fix before it shipped, which had made the class-name match look for a doubly-quoted name so that no real row matched at all. The classifier has now been wrong four times and every one of those defects would have passed a green run; tools/checker_validation_classifier.sh is the twelve shapes that hold it, including one constructed from the engine source because no run of this case can produce it.
